about.title: Personal Injury Help in Hanford, California
about.longDescription: Hanford is a close-knit Kings County community, but like any city with steady traffic, it sees its share of collisions. In the most recent reporting year, Hanford recorded 80 injury collisions and 107 people injured — a reminder that everyday trips down N 11th Avenue, 12th Avenue, N 10th Avenue, and 11th Avenue can turn into something far more serious in an instant. Whether you were rear-ended near a busy corridor, injured as a pedestrian, or hurt in a fall, the aftermath often brings medical bills, missed work, and confusion about what to do next. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people in Hanford with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of what happened and explain the options available under California law. There's no cost to reach out, and attorneys in this network only get paid if you recover compensation. You don't have to figure this out alone or guess at deadlines and paperwork. Reaching out costs nothing, and it may help you understand where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity is involved. Talking to someone early helps make sure you don't miss a deadline.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be Clear-Cut
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover compensation even if you were partly at fault — your share of fault just reduces the amount, it doesn't erase your claim.

items.title: No Cap on Certain Damages
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in ordinary injury cases, which means your claim isn't automatically limited to medical bills and lost wages.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to You
items.desc: Attorneys in this network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover money. There's no retainer or hourly fee to worry about while you focus on recovering.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: In most personal injury cases, you have two years from the date of the incident to file a lawsuit. If a government agency is involved, that window can be as short as six months, so it's worth getting information sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your recovery amount would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Hanford?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher volumes of reported crashes along N 11th Avenue, 12th Avenue, N 10th Avenue, and 11th Avenue, with reports also tending to peak on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are neutral counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does it cost anything to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent personal injury attorneys. We don't provide legal representation ourselves.
